title: Merge/prune overcomplete experts, then recover logical roles with compact Views
hypothesis: After a routing-weighted merge/prune identifies a compact physical expert pool, rank-1 role Views recover removed distinctions with lower complete bytes than independent experts and materially lower heldout error than merge-only, prune-only, and small-from-start controls.

synthetic_task.importance: cluster-skewed routing frequencies; one low-frequency expert in each cluster has a larger private residual

development.selection: fixed rank-1 residual view; no hyperparameter sweep

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after exact native low-rank alias or failure of the development quality/storage gate.

controls: prune-only top-2 important experts with nearest retained routing
merged core plus learned rank-1 logical View
merged core plus native rank-1 residual factorization
pass_gate: Mirror test nRMSE <=0.02; at least 25% fewer complete bytes than independent; strictly lower heldout error than merge-only and prune-only at no more active compute; and no exact native-control alias.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific claim if native low-rank exactly aliases Mirror, quality gate misses, bytes savings <25%, or simple merge/prune control matches quality with lower bytes/compute.

compute.active_macs_per_example: count dense expert apply plus router score proxy; report reconstruction separately
compute.wall_time: single small CPU operator-evaluation calibration; not throughput evidence

boundaries: Synthetic Gaussian inputs and linear experts only; no trained MoE, language-model, GPU, or general REAP/MC-SMoE claim.
Small-from-start control is represented by the same two cluster means without overcomplete teacher exposure; this screen does not compare training trajectories.
Mirror View is rank-1 residual factorization; exact equality to its native control ends attribution testing.
